title: Full Stack Developer
description:
**Role: Full Stack Developer / SDE**  
**Experience: 3-6 years**  
**Location: Indore**  
**Type: Full time**

**About the role:**  
We are keeping this as one role rather than two because most of our work cuts vertically. A change to how a run reports its state touches the runtime, the API contract and three screens. Splitting that across two people at our size produces handoffs, not speed.

The AI layer is only as trustworthy as the plumbing under it and only as usable as the surface over it. This role owns both.

**What you will own:**  
**Backend and platform**

* FastAPI services across the Control and Agent Runtime planes.
* The agent runtime harness — the generic stateless worker that loads a kit and becomes that agent for the length of one run.

title: Java Developer
description:
**About QPC**

QPC is a UK-headquartered contact centre technology company. QPC gives contact centres a real-time view of their operations. It collects events from major CX platforms such as Genesys, Amazon Connect, NICE, Avaya and Talkdesk and brings them into one platform for live reporting, workforce management and AI-driven insight. QPC has offices in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, North America, India and Australia.

**Role Summary**

We are hiring a Java developer to work alongside QPC's India team in Bangalore to build and maintain the event adapters that convert contact centre platform events into QPC's normalised event model. In general, you will work from a clear, pre-written design produced by our Event Adapter Analyst, which defines the incoming record structure, the events and attributes that matter, and the sequences needed to track a contact. Your job is to turn that design into robust, well-tested Java that fits into our existing collection service.

Collecting data from the source platform (APIs, polling, streams, webhooks) is a separate concern from converting it into events. Where collection has been decoupled, your adapter simply receives events from a queue such as NATS JetStream and does not need to worry about how they got there.

title: AWS & DevOps Engineer
description:
We are looking for an AWS DevOps Engineer to run and scale the infrastructure behind our EdTech platform for JEE, NEET, and board-exam aspirants. Our stack is a set of NestJS microservices on multi-AZ EKS, backed by Aurora MySQL with RDS Proxy, MongoDB, Redis, and OpenSearch, serving a Next.js website, a Laravel admin panel, and native Android and iOS apps.

The interesting part of this job is the load pattern. Traffic is not flat — it spikes hard and predictably around live classes, test launches, and exam season, with tens of thousands of concurrent students hitting the platform in the same ten-minute window. You will own the systems that have to stay up in exactly those windows, where a five-minute outage during a live test is a real cost to real students.

This is a hands-on ownership role, not a ticket-closing role. You will build, automate, monitor, and be on the hook when something breaks.

**What You'll Do**

* Own and operate our AWS production environment — EKS, EC2, ALB/NLB, VPC and networking, S3, CloudFront, Route 53, IAM, and the managed data services behind them.
* Run our Kubernetes workloads on EKS — deployments, autoscaling (HPA, Cluster Autoscaler/Karpenter), resource limits, node groups, ingress, and rollout strategies that do not drop traffic.
* Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines with Jenkins and Git — automated builds, tests, image builds, and safe deploys across dev, staging, and production for backend services, web, and mobile release artifacts.
